I was planning on having the object either float extremely close to the researcher at all times, with it being impossible to move farther than a certain distance away without causing him physical harm. item.title: Re: Singularity - Seeking Greenlight (1/2)
item.content:encoded:
I think overall this idea/thread is nice but I have some slight concerns.

Open
Close

What I think is great

  • The story you want to bring seems to have been thought through and definitely has some depth. You also mentioned how you plan on doing that (mostly logs and interviews) which is great. I also think the theme of guilt and your narrative compliment each other nicely.
  • I think the initial contact would make for a great discovery/addendum/…
  • You said you wanted the origin and purpose open ended which in my opinion fits the abilities and adds to the mystery of the SCP. It also makes sense since you mentioned that you plan to build more upon this in future tales and articles.

What concerns me

  • I'm interested in how you would describe/mention how the SCP clings to the researcher. It is a bit unclear to me if you will mention this quickly or rather in detail in one of the addenda.
  • The abilities that influence time in some way or form are great but I am concerned that you will overdo it. Honestly, I'm not great with these themes/things but please know that there is a difference between complex and overcomplicated. As someone who tends to do the later I recommend you type it but always check if it affects the readability afterwards.

Final verdict
I compliment you for trying the combination of a guilt/isolation theme, possible time-travel,… and I think the foundations of this idea are solid but some things need a bit fleshing out.

I think this and the concerns in this thread can all be solved by drafting in a sandbox with a good amount of commitment, time and critique. I also advise you to check the chat and draft forums for additional help should you need it. That being said, here is a second greenlight so you can use the draft forum. (I have an author page.)

Good luck with your SCP.

item.title: Re: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Wow, thank you so much! Both for the greenlight and the amazing ideas!

The backstory of the anomaly is something that I don't have completely fleshed out right now. My intention is for the anomaly to represent sudden tragedy and existential dread in this article. I do however eventually want to reveal in a future article or tale that it was no accident that the SCP landed in front of this researcher.

I had planned to just allow the researcher to be able to stop time, as I didn't want to him to be able to go back and change what happened. However, the idea of him being able to go back in time, but only messing things up further is a really interesting idea that plays into the theme. I wanted to have a theme mirroring real life where what's done is done, so I don't know if I'll incorporate this, but great suggestion.

I am planning on having a record of a Keter class containment breach with zero casualties due to the researcher stopping time and moving everyone to safety. Afterwards, he realizes the potential his powers have to help others. This, along with maybe a good word from Glass, is what convinces the foundation higher ups to not contain him like an SCP.

item.title: Re: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hello!
Interesting SCP You've got there!
It would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So….
Wow….
I love it!
That narrative is so creative! It's such a simple concept, but you really expand on it in a way not many first-time writers do! The arc that you have would make a pretty emotional and insightful story if written correctly. My only concern is that I think the researcher would likely end up as an anomaly himself (or classified as one, at least), and may end up contained. Here are a few plotpoints I'd like to suggest

  • Does the researcher have any specific reason he connected with the anomaly? It just seems a bit random it would scan him for no reason and then just attatch to him.
  • How does he help others with the anomaly, if I may ask? Can he reverse time? Or jump forward with it? How would this help the foundation?
  • Maybe he can try to use the hourglass to go back and try to save the researchers? But maybe he ends up killing more people in the process or creating a paradox or changing reality alltogether (think "Flashpoint")
  • Perhaps using the
  • Maybe the hourglass literally breaks reality or puts the user in a loop that only he can recognize. Maybe have a repeating interview w/ Doctor glass, where each time Glass steps into the room and talks to the researcher, something is wrong.(i.e. Glass has snakes coming out of his head, the paint is the wrong color, the table is made of meatballs) And each time the researcher notices this, have the loop repeat.
  • What if the researcher went haywire? He tries locking out the guilt, and starts to think of himself as a god, reigning destruction upon the world, only for him to snap back to his senses and try to return everything to normal, only for it to break

Those are just a view ideas. But in the meantime, have a Greenlight. Best of luck on the SCP, and please let me know if you have any advice/questions/concerns about what I've said.

item.title: Singularity - Requesting Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional and symbolic, with undertones of mystery and light comedic moments

Page Layout: Traditional, with an account of the recovery, and addendum containing testing logs, and a few interviews.

Elevator Pitch: A mysterious black, metal object resembling an hourglass appears in the sky above a foundation site and crashes through the roof. The object appears to consume the time of living beings near it, causing them to leap forward in time and age accordingly. The object ends up killing several researchers, but one seems to be unaffected. The object later even goes as far as to attach itself to him. This researcher then has to grapple with survivor's guilt, and must learn to keep moving forward, accepting both the good and the bad of the object being attached to him.

+ Additional Details
- Additional Details

Central Narrative: (Ultimately, I want to tell a human story about a man initially struggling with guilt, but with the help of a friend, is able to accept the way things are and work to move forward. I'd also like to work in themes of overcoming fate and unfortunate circumstances.) After crashing into a foundation site, the SCP lands near a researcher. After the anomaly is contained, the research wants to learn more about it, and is appointed head researcher. During a routine examination, the SCP activates, while our main researcher and two others are in the room. The two other researchers are killed by the SCP, but our main researcher is left. Later, the SCP permanently attaches itself to him. Through interviews with Dr. Glass, we learn he is suffering from survivor’s guilt and isolation. During subsequent testing, we find out that the SCP can allow the researcher to exist outside of time. (Time stop) The end of the arc will have the researcher coming to terms with the conflict he feels towards the SCP being attached to him and using it to help the foundation/the world, while leaving the origin and purpose of the SCP open ended.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: In addition to a relatable human struggle, throughout the article, there’s hints here and there that the SCP may have been intentionally created by an unknown group or individual.

Additional Notes: I’m hoping to expand on the backstory of the SCP in future tales or articles, as well as feature the researcher in some of my future articles. While I couldn’t explain every detail here, I have the main arc of the story pretty well thought out. I’d also like to show that it was no accident the anomaly bonded to this researcher. Critique and greenlights welcome.
